title: What If Every Mosquito on Earth Vanished Tomorrow?

scenes.text: What if every mosquito vanished tonight? One disease ecologist suspects most people wouldn't notice.
Mosquito-borne diseases kill over 700,000 people a year. Malaria alone killed about 597,000 in 2023.
Those deaths would drop, mostly in Africa, where about 95 percent of malaria deaths happen.
But there are around 3,500 mosquito species, and they feed fish, dragonflies, turtles and songbirds.
Males mostly drink nectar, so some species also pollinate flowers, including orchids.
But researchers admit they don't fully understand mosquitoes' role in food webs, so the full effects are unknown.

description:
What if every mosquito on Earth vanished?
It could save hundreds of thousands of lives a year, but scientists say the ecological effects are hard to predict.
